## Order physical fills, exchange and corner refresh (`apply_boundaries; exchange_ghost_zones`) {#sec-ch14-timing}

### Summary

Two fillers write ghosts and their footprints overlap at the corners of a block. The physical callbacks own
the ghost slabs of physical faces, the whole orthogonal extent included; the exchange owns the slabs of
layout faces, corners excluded when `skip_corner` is on except an $x_2$–$x_3$ corner under the diagonal corner rule
(@sec-ch14-exchange). A corner slab that lies in a physical x1 face's
ghost region and in a tangential layout face's ghost region is written by the exchange with the neighbour's
column, after which the x1 wall of that column has to be re-imposed. This scheme states the order in which
the two fillers run and the refresh that keeps the overlap consistent.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Order physical fills and exchanged-corner refresh.

**Data.** Hydro state and tracers in their current representation.

**Placement.** Driver order differs between block and mesh stepping.

**Activation.** Automatic with the driver; no independent YAML switch.

**Guarantee / limits.** Refresh requires idempotent callbacks and excludes outflow.

**Evidence.** Report checks and source-test limits are in the Tests layer.
:::

### Derivation

This is an operator-order contract. Copying neighbour values and applying a physical wall need not commute
at their overlap: the exchange overwrites a wall corner with the neighbour's interior column. Re-applying
the wall map to the newly exchanged strip restores the same parity relation as on the owned strip, provided
the callback reads only interior values and is idempotent. The registry contract (`BC_FUNCTION`,
{{< code src/bc/bc_func.hpp BC_FUNCTION >}}) and the `refresh` closure of
`MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_exchange.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}})
encode these requirements. Check C1 includes a two-dimensional corner where an exchange overwrites a prior
mirror and a second fill restricted to the exchanged strip restores parity; this is an exact discrete
ownership check, not a convergence proof [check `src/snapy_report/ch14/checks/boundary_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch14/checks/boundary_check.out`]. The checks do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

Initialization (`MeshBlockImpl::initialize`, {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize >}})
runs `initialize_under_mesh` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize_under_mesh >}}):
`initialize_local` captures the outflow background before any physical fill and then fills the primitives;
`exchange_state` exchanges the primitives and the scalar ratios with `interpolate` on; and
`finalize_initialization` converts to conserved variables, records the solid fill states and fills the conserved
fields.

A stage runs as the list of ops that `StageExecutor::build_schedule`
({{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::build_schedule >}}) builds: for a bare block, a stage-entry
exchange first; then `advance`, `forcing`[^rg-51c00aae93ad], `combine`, `saturation`, `chemistry` and `boundaries`. So in the block
driver (`MeshBlockImpl::forward`, {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::forward >}}) a change made
between calls reaches the ghosts before reconstruction. A Mesh block's schedule has no exchange op:
`MeshImpl::forward` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}) runs every block's stage (a registered
chemistry step runs in the last stage there, before the `boundaries` op, as on a bare block), then its global phase (the
axial-momentum closure, followed by the physical fills), and exchanges the blocks last. Within the stage, `stage_combine` refills the solid hydro cells after the RK[^rg-45f96bd373b5]
combination, the `saturation` op runs the saturation adjustment on the last stage, and the `boundaries` op
(`MeshBlockImpl::stage_boundaries`, {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_boundaries >}})
runs the physical fills of `apply_boundaries`.

The refresh in `exchange_ghost_zones` walks every installed callback except outflow. An $x_2$ or $x_3$ callback
takes part only when its own face is physical, and "physical" here excludes a callback whose name starts with
`periodic` and, on a cubed-sphere block, the built-in `custom` no-op of an $x_2$ or $x_3$ face. Each callback is
restricted to the tangential ghost slabs whose face is not physical. Each slab is $\min(n_g,
\lfloor n/2\rfloor)$ cells wide in the tangential direction, with $n$ that direction's extent. A callback whose name
starts with `reflecting` is instead called once over the full extent when no tangential face is physical: it mirrors
each row from that row's own interior, so the one call writes the slabs and rewrites the other ghost rows with the
values they already hold. The conserved hydro state and the scalar densities are refreshed, and the scalar
primitive ratios are then recomputed from them. Auxiliary fields take the same two-step order: the donor factor of
the flux positivity limiter is exchanged raw and then passed through every installed callback with scalar type
(`flux_positivity_sync_theta_`, {{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_sync_theta_ >}}), called by
`PositivityLimiter::sync_` for the species and by the `sync_theta` closure of `ScalarImpl::forward`
({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}) for the passive scalars. No accuracy order follows from
this sequence; the wall-rest and phase-change tests are the available assertions.

### Code

**How to use.** This fragment selects the physical callback, not the schedule. Initialize through the driver and
retain its stage loop. Changes between block `forward` calls reach the next reconstruction through its leading
exchange.

This is a configuration fragment, not a standalone simulation deck.

```yaml
boundary-condition:
  external:
    x1-inner: reflecting
    x1-outer: reflecting
```

**Refusals and prerequisites.** There is no timing YAML switch and no independent schedule validator. The callback
contract forbids dependence on the full tangential extent. Outflow is deliberately excluded from corner refresh
because it needs full-size saved backgrounds.

**Read the implementation.** The schedule builder contains these lines
({{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::build_schedule >}}):

```cpp
  if (!block_at(block)->_mesh_executor) {
    Op exchange;
    exchange.name = "exchange";
```

These lines put the stage-entry exchange first for a bare block, which implements the block-driver ownership
order in the Derivation layer. A Mesh block has no such op; the Mesh exchanges after the stages, as documented
above.

: Implementation sites for timing. {#tbl-ch14-timing-code}

1. Initialize: capture the outflow background, fill the primitives, exchange them, convert, fill the conserved
   fields. The anchor `boundary_reference_w` is in
   {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize_local >}}.
2. Use the order of the selected driver; the two drivers do not place their exchange at the same point. The
   anchor `run_stage` is in {{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}.
3. After a block exchange, refresh the wall corners in the conserved and scalar representations and
   recompute the scalar ratios. The anchor `refresh` is in
   {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_exchange.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}.
4. At stage end, fill the physical faces after the solid refill, the saturation adjustment and the chemistry.
   The anchor `apply_boundaries` is in {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_boundaries >}}.

|---|---|---|---|

| `test_wall_saturation.release` | Boundary phase change conserves energy and water | relative error below $10^{-12}$ | test constant |
| `boundary_check.py` (report only) | `[C1]` as described below | exact | symbolic, rational or integer identity |

and the scalar corner check is

The conservation assertions are in

Device/rank distinctions and missing runs are recorded in @sec-ch16-ch11.

exactly.[^ch11-timing-run]

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Outflow is excluded from the refresh: an outflow face keeps the exchanged corner, because its background is sized
for the full block and it needs primitives. The public
`MeshImpl::exchange_ghost_zones` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}) only builds
the sync options and calls the exchange, so a caller cannot assume it supplies the block method's refresh. A
custom callback that depends on the full orthogonal shape of its input violates the documented contract and
is not refreshed correctly.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result
is claimed.
:::
